sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.
Heard Mr. Dharm K. Raval, learned advocate for the applicant.
Mr. Rathin Raval, learned advocate has entered his appearance on behalf of the respondent no.5 - insurance company.

2. The present application is filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act read with Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking condonation of delay of 204 days caused in preferring the appeal.

3. Learned advocate for the applicant has mainly relied upon the averments made in the application and has submitted that thought the impugned order is pronounced on NEUTRAL CITATION Vinodkumar Parsottambhai Prajapati vs Jivanbhai Bbabhai Patni on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/153776878/
1 C/CA/1368/2025 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined 29th April, 2024, the applicant having sustained serious injuries and having lost his leg, was unable to walk properly or to attend his daily work.

entities.text: NEUTRAL CITATION Vinodkumar Parsottambhai Prajapati vs Jivanbhai Bbabhai Patni
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He was apprised about the award being passed by the advocate on record only in the month of June, 2024.
The applicant having received copy of the award was not satisfied by the compensation awarded.

It is further pointed-out that the insurance company had also approached in appeal and the applicant was served with the notice of admission in the month of August, 2024 whereby the amount was directed to be deposited before the concerned Tribunal and is permitted to be withdrawn in November, 2024.
Upon receipt of the aforesaid amount, necessary arrangement is made to engage a lawyer to approach in appeal.
By referring to the aforesaid, learned advocate has submitted that meanwhile, the delay of 204 days had crept in.

He has therefore submitted that all through-out, the applicant was in process of pursuing the remedy of appeal, however, because of the unavoidable circumstances and the treatment, which he was required to undergo, could not approach in appeal within a period of limitation.
He has therefore, urged this Court to take liberal approach and condone the delay.
4. Mr. Rathin Raval, learned advocate for the respondent - insurance company has vehemently objected to the aforesaid submissions of the learned advocate for the applicant.

According to him,
no sufficient cause is made-out to consider the condonation of delay of huge days.

5. Having heard learned advocates for the respective parties and having examined the aforesaid facts, this Court NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/1368/2025 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined has a reason to believe the aforesaid circumstances pointed- out by the learned advocate for the applicant.
In the opinion of this Court, sufficient cause has been made-out to consider the prayer of codonation of delay.
Hence, present application stands allowed.
The delay of 204 days caused in preferring the appeal is hereby condoned.
Rule made absolute.
(NISHA M. THAKORE, J.) AMAR RATHOD...
